cards.headline: Lalezari 2001 (pooled analysis, high-risk patients): zanamivir gave a 2.5-day treatment benefit, return to normal activities 3.0 days earlier, and a 43% relative reduction in complications requiring antibiotics
cards.summary: Lalezari 2001 (pooled analysis, high-risk patients): zanamivir gave a 2.5-day treatment benefit, return to normal activities 3.0 days earlier, and a 43% relative reduction in complications requiring antibiotics
cards.type: Retrospective pooled analysis of randomised placebo-controlled trials, high-risk subgroup
cards.people: Retrospective pooled analysis of randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trials completed before or during the 1998–1999 season: 2,751 patients recruited in total, of whom 321 (12%) were high-risk (elderly or chronically ill) and 154 of those were randomised to inhaled zanamivir 10 mg twice daily for 5 days for confirmed influenza, with 21- to 28-day follow-up.
cards.result: High-risk patients on zanamivir had a treatment benefit of 2.5 days on median time to alleviation of influenza symptoms versus placebo (P=0.015), returned to normal activities 3.0 days earlier (P=0.022), and had an 11% reduction (P=0.039) in median total symptom score over days 1 to 5 relative to placebo. Zanamivir reduced the incidence of complications requiring antibiotic use by 43% relative to placebo (P=0.045) — a relative measure; the absolute complication incidences are not printed in the fetched record. Adverse events were of similar nature and frequency in the two groups.
cards.watchOut: A pooled analysis, not a dedicated high-risk trial: only 321 of 2,751 programme patients were high-risk, the analysis is retrospective, and the 43% complication figure is relative with no absolute rates in the record — do not convert it into an absolute benefit.
cards.source: Lalezari J et al. Zanamivir for the treatment of influenza A and B infection in high-risk patients: a pooled analysis of randomized controlled trials. shelves.title: Favipiravir for uncomplicated influenza: SPLIT — one phase 3 trial cut illness by 14.4 hours, the other did not; antiviral effect consistent, symptom benefit inconsistent
shelves.question: In adults with uncomplicated influenza, does oral favipiravir versus placebo — or versus standard neuraminidase/baloxavir therapy — shorten time to symptom alleviation?
shelves.mesh: Adult · Humans · Influenza, Human · Pyrazines · Antiviral Agents · Double-Blind Method · Fever · RNA · Treatment Outcome · Amides
shelves.balance: SPLIT. The two phase 3 placebo-controlled trials, reported in ONE publication, disagree on the clinical endpoint: US316 found a significant 14.4-hour reduction in time to illness alleviation (median 84.2 vs 98.6 hours, P=0.004), while US317 found no significant reduction (77.8 vs 83.9 hours); both showed clear antiviral effects (reduced viral titres, RNA load and time to virus detection, P<0.001). A post-hoc exposure analysis of those same trials found 41–43% of favipiravir recipients never reached the target average minimum concentration of 20 µg/mL, and those who did had larger antiviral effects. The AD ASTRA platform trial (944 randomised; favipiravir arm 223) is open-label and virological: favipiravir accelerated viral clearance by 66% relative to no study drug but was 10% slower than baloxavir with non-inferiority not shown, and time to resolution of all symptoms did not differ significantly. On the STRATOS convention the two phase 3 trials count as one publication, so the floor here is three reports covering four trials — stated on the face. Favipiravir is not licensed for influenza in the US or EU (licensed in Japan under restricted conditions), and its embryotoxicity warning is part of the real-world answer.

cards.headline: Hayden 2022 (two phase 3 trials, one publication): US316 — favipiravir cut time to illness alleviation by 14.4 hours (84.2 vs 98.6 h, P=0.004); US317 — no significant reduction (77.8 vs 83.9 h)
cards.summary: Hayden 2022 (two phase 3 trials, one publication): US316 — favipiravir cut time to illness alleviation by 14.4 hours (84.2 vs 98.6 h, P=0.004); US317 — no significant reduction (77.8 vs 83.9 h)
cards.type: Two phase 3 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trials reported in one publication (US316 and US317)
cards.people: Otherwise healthy adults with influenza-like symptoms and fever of 48 hours or less, randomised double-blind to favipiravir 1800 mg twice daily on day 1 then 800 mg twice daily on days 2–5, or placebo: US316 — 301 favipiravir, 322 placebo (1:1); US317 — 526 favipiravir, 169 placebo (3:1). Primary endpoint: time to illness alleviation (6 influenza symptoms absent or mild and fever absent) in intention-to-treat influenza-infected participants.
cards.result: US316: favipiravir was associated with a 14.4-hour reduction in median time to illness alleviation versus placebo (84.2 vs 98.6 hours; P=0.004). US317: favipiravir did not significantly reduce time to alleviation (median 77.8 vs 83.9 hours). In both trials favipiravir reduced viral titres, viral RNA load area under the curve over days 1–5, and median time to cessation of virus detection (P<0.001). Aside from asymptomatic hyperuricaemia, no important differences in adverse events were found. The authors describe significant antiviral efficacy but inconsistent illness alleviation at this dosing regimen.
cards.watchOut: Two trials but ONE publication — counted as one report for the evidence floor, as the commissioning row directs. The clinical endpoint split (one positive, one negative trial) is the central fact of this shelf and is not pooled away.
cards.source: Hayden FG et al. Favipiravir Treatment of Uncomplicated Influenza in Adults: Results of Two Phase 3, Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trials. cards.headline: Hayden 2024 (exposure–pharmacodynamic report OF the phase 3 programme): 41–43% of favipiravir recipients failed to reach the target average Cmin of 20 µg/mL; those who reached it had larger antiviral effects
cards.summary: Hayden 2024 (exposure–pharmacodynamic report OF the phase 3 programme): 41–43% of favipiravir recipients failed to reach the target average Cmin of 20 µg/mL; those who reached it had larger antiviral effects
cards.type: Programme report: post-hoc exposure–pharmacodynamic analysis of the two phase 3 trials (same programme as the card above — not independent comparative evidence)
cards.people: Adults with uncomplicated influenza randomised in the same two phase 3 trials (favipiravir n=827, placebo n=419 in the pharmacokinetic sampling population), with serial plasma samples; post-hoc analyses assessed reaching an average minimum concentration (Cmin) of at least 20 µg/mL and its association with antiviral efficacy. A report OF the phase 3 programme, not a separate trial.
cards.result: Favipiravir concentrations varied widely between individuals, and the regimen failed to reach an average Cmin above 20 µg/mL in 41–43% of participants. Those attaining the threshold showed greater reductions in nasopharyngeal infectious virus titres on days 2 and 3 and lower viral titre area under the curve than those who did not; those below the threshold had over 2-fold higher metabolite (T-705M1) to favipiravir ratios and were more likely to weigh over 80 kg (61.5–64%). Higher exposure was also associated with more rapid illness alleviation compared with placebo and with lower-exposure favipiravir recipients.
cards.watchOut: Post-hoc and exposure-stratified: patients who reach a drug level differ from those who do not, so the exposure–effect association is hypothesis-generating, not a randomised dose comparison. It explains a possible reason for the phase 3 split; it does not resolve it.
cards.source: Hayden FG et al. Oral Favipiravir Exposure and Pharmacodynamic Effects in Adult Outpatients With Acute Influenza. The Journal of infectious diseases. 2024. PMID: 37739792. Registry ID: NCT01728753; NCT01068912. cards.headline: AD ASTRA 2026 (phase 2 platform trial): favipiravir accelerated viral clearance by 66% relative to no study drug, was 10% slower than baloxavir (non-inferiority not shown), and did not significantly shorten time to resolution of all symptoms
cards.summary: AD ASTRA 2026 (phase 2 platform trial): favipiravir accelerated viral clearance by 66% relative to no study drug, was 10% slower than baloxavir (non-inferiority not shown), and did not significantly shorten time to resolution of all symptoms
cards.type: Phase 2 open-label adaptive randomised platform trial (AD ASTRA), favipiravir vs baloxavir vs oseltamivir vs no study drug
cards.people: 944 patients aged 18–60 years with acute influenza (4 days of symptoms or less) at low risk of progression, in Thailand, Laos, Nepal and Brazil, randomised open-label to baloxavir (199), favipiravir (223; modified intention-to-treat 196), oseltamivir (200), no study drug (228), or another intervention reported separately (94). Favipiravir dosing: 1800 mg loading dose, 1800 mg 12 hours later, then 800 mg twice daily for 4 days. Primary endpoint: rate of oropharyngeal influenza viral RNA clearance, days 0–5.
cards.result: Compared with no study drug, viral clearance rates were accelerated by 86% (95% credible interval 60 to 117) with baloxavir, 66% (45 to 94) with favipiravir and 49% (28 to 74) with oseltamivir — relative clearance-rate increases, with the posterior probability of at least a 20% relative increase 1.0 for all three. Compared with baloxavir, favipiravir was 10% slower on clearance (95% CrI −4 to 22) and non-inferiority could not be shown (posterior probability 0.55). Median time to fever resolution was accelerated with all three antivirals versus no study drug (absolute differences 0.5 to 0.9 days), whereas time to resolution of all symptoms was not significantly different between groups. Thirty-one grade 3-or-above adverse events occurred, five severe (one in the favipiravir group).
cards.watchOut: Open-label, phase 2 and virological in orientation, in low-risk patients aged 18–60: it ranks antiviral activity, it is not a third placebo-controlled efficacy trial, and its symptom-resolution endpoint was not significantly different between groups.
cards.source: Jittamala P et al. Baloxavir marboxil, favipiravir, or oseltamivir in patients with non-severe symptomatic seasonal influenza (AD ASTRA): a phase 2, open-label, adaptive, randomised controlled trial. The Lancet. cards.headline: Synthesis: SPLIT — consistent antiviral activity, inconsistent symptom benefit: one phase 3 trial positive by 14.4 hours, one negative, and a platform trial positive on viral clearance but not on symptom resolution
cards.summary: Synthesis: SPLIT — consistent antiviral activity, inconsistent symptom benefit: one phase 3 trial positive by 14.4 hours, one negative, and a platform trial positive on viral clearance but not on symptom resolution
cards.type: Synthesis
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf (two phase 3 trials in one publication, their post-hoc exposure analysis, and the AD ASTRA platform trial).
cards.result: Favipiravir at 1800 mg twice daily on day 1 then 800 mg twice daily clearly reduces viral titres and shedding in uncomplicated influenza, but the patient-facing endpoint — time to illness alleviation — was significantly shortened in only one of the two phase 3 trials, and AD ASTRA found no significant difference in time to resolution of all symptoms. Underexposure (41–43% below the target concentration) is a plausible contributor, unproven as the explanation. Regulatory status is part of the answer: not licensed for influenza in the US/EU, restricted licensing in Japan, with an embryotoxicity warning.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each trial's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Laninamivir for post-exposure prophylaxis: single 40 mg dose cut household influenza to 4.5% vs 12.1% on placebo; 11% vs 19% in children — Japan-only programme
shelves.question: In household contacts of an influenza patient (adults and children), does a single inhaled dose — or two daily doses — of laninamivir octanoate versus placebo prevent influenza illness?
shelves.mesh: Administration, Inhalation · Adolescent · Adult · Antiviral Agents · Child · Double-Blind Method · Enzyme Inhibitors · Family Characteristics · Female · Guanidines · Humans · Influenza, Human · Male · Middle Aged · Neuraminidase · Post-Exposure Prophylaxis · Pyrans · Sialic Acids · Young Adult · Zanamivir
shelves.balance: LIKELY (benefit), on three Japanese household-contact trials from a single development programme — the single-programme structure is stated on the face. Clinical influenza over 10 days: 3.9% (20 mg for 2 days) and 3.7% (20 mg for 3 days) versus 16.9% on placebo in 1,451 analysed contacts — relative risk reductions of 77.0% and 78.1% relative; a single 40 mg dose gave 4.5% versus 12.1% on placebo (relative risk reduction 62.8% relative) in 801 analysed contacts; and in children under 10, a single 20 mg dose gave 11% versus 19% (relative risk reduction 45.8% relative). Adverse events were similar to placebo in all three trials. All effect measures are relative risks of influenza illness and are labelled relative, with the absolute rates beside them on every card. Laninamivir is licensed in Japan only. Cross-point: laninamivir TREATMENT is a different question, homed at pack #7208 — its studies are not re-carded here, and the two shelves are not merged.

cards.summary: Kashiwagi 2013: laninamivir 20 mg daily for 2 or 3 days cut clinical influenza in household contacts to 3.9% and 3.7% versus 16.9% on placebo (relative risk reductions 77.0% and 78.1% relative)
cards.type: Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial, laninamivir 20 mg × 2 or 3 days vs placebo for post-exposure prophylaxis
cards.people: Household members without influenza in contact with an influenza-infected index patient, randomised double-blind (1:1:1) to laninamivir octanoate 20 mg once daily for 2 days, 20 mg once daily for 3 days, or placebo: 1,711 participants enrolled, 1,451 included in the primary analysis. Primary endpoint: proportion developing clinical influenza during a 10-day period.
cards.result: Clinical influenza developed in 3.9% (19/487) on the 2-day regimen, 3.7% (18/486) on the 3-day regimen and 16.9% (81/478) on placebo (P<0.001 for each laninamivir group versus placebo). The relative risk reductions versus placebo were 77.0% (95% CI 62.7 to 85.8) and 78.1% (95% CI 64.1 to 86.7) relative — absolute rates 3.9% and 3.7% versus 16.9%, as printed above. Adverse event incidences in the laninamivir groups were similar to placebo.
cards.watchOut: Japanese household-contact trial from the laninamivir development programme; 1,711 enrolled but 1,451 analysed. The 2-day and 3-day regimens performed identically — the extra day added nothing measurable.
cards.source: Kashiwagi S et al. Laninamivir octanoate for post-exposure prophylaxis of influenza in household contacts: a randomized double blind placebo controlled trial. Journal of infection and chemotherapy : official journal of the Japan Society of Chemotherapy. 2013. PMID: 23732307. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Kashiwagi 2016: a SINGLE 40 mg inhaled dose worked as prophylaxis — clinical influenza 4.5% versus 12.1% on placebo (relative risk reduction 62.8% relative, P=0.001)
cards.summary: Kashiwagi 2016: a SINGLE 40 mg inhaled dose worked as prophylaxis — clinical influenza 4.5% versus 12.1% on placebo (relative risk reduction 62.8% relative, P=0.001)
cards.type: Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial, single-dose laninamivir 40 mg vs 20 mg × 2 days vs placebo for post-exposure prophylaxis
cards.people: 803 participants who had cohabited with an influenza patient within 48 hours of the patient's symptom onset, randomised double-blind (1:1:1) to a single administration of laninamivir octanoate 40 mg, laninamivir 20 mg once daily for 2 days, or placebo; 801 included in the primary analysis. Primary endpoint: proportion developing clinical influenza (virus-positive, axillary temperature above 37.5°C and at least 2 symptoms) over 10 days.
cards.result: Clinical influenza developed in 4.5% (12/267) on single-dose 40 mg, 4.5% (13/269) on 20 mg for 2 days and 12.1% (32/265) on placebo. A single 40 mg administration significantly reduced influenza development versus placebo (P=0.001); the relative risk reductions versus placebo were 62.8% and 63.1% relative for the single-dose and 2-day groups respectively — absolute rates 4.5% versus 12.1%, as printed above. Adverse events were similar across the groups.
cards.watchOut: Same Japanese development programme and overlapping investigator group as the 2013 trial — supportive programme evidence, not an independent replication by a different group. Registry ID is the Japanese JapicCTI number printed in the record.

cards.headline: Nakano 2016 (children under 10): a single 20 mg dose reduced clinical influenza to 11% versus 19% on placebo (relative risk reduction 45.8% relative, P=0.02) — 343 children
cards.summary: Nakano 2016 (children under 10): a single 20 mg dose reduced clinical influenza to 11% versus 19% on placebo (relative risk reduction 45.8% relative, P=0.02) — 343 children
cards.type: Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial in children, single-dose laninamivir 20 mg vs placebo for post-exposure prophylaxis
cards.people: 343 children under 10 years of age without influenza, living in the same household as an influenza-infected index case, randomised double-blind (1:1) to a single inhaled dose of laninamivir octanoate 20 mg or placebo; 341 included in the full analysis set. Primary endpoint: proportion developing clinical influenza during a 10-day period.
cards.result: Clinical influenza developed in 11% (18/171) of the laninamivir group and 19% (33/170) of the placebo group (P=0.02). The relative risk reduction was 45.8% relative (95% CI 7.5% to 68.2%) — absolute rates 11% versus 19%, as printed above. The incidence of adverse events was similar in both groups. The authors conclude a single 20 mg dose was effective and well tolerated as prophylaxis in these children.
cards.watchOut: The paediatric effect is smaller than the adult programme's (45.8% relative risk reduction, with a wide confidence interval from 7.5% to 68.2%) and the absolute difference is 8 percentage points — read the relative and absolute figures together. Same Japanese programme.
cards.source: Nakano T et al. Inhaled Laninamivir Octanoate as Prophylaxis for Influenza in Children. Pediatrics. 2016. PMID: 27940664. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: three household-contact trials, one programme — laninamivir prophylaxis consistently and substantially reduced clinical influenza, with a single 40 mg dose performing as well as multi-day regimens
cards.summary: Synthesis: three household-contact trials, one programme — laninamivir prophylaxis consistently and substantially reduced clinical influenza, with a single 40 mg dose performing as well as multi-day regimens
cards.type: Synthesis
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf (1,451 and 801 analysed contacts, and 341 analysed children).
cards.result: Every carded trial favoured laninamivir octanoate over placebo on the same 10-day clinical-influenza endpoint: absolute rates 3.9%/3.7% versus 16.9% (multi-day adult regimens), 4.5% versus 12.1% (single 40 mg dose) and 11% versus 19% (children, single 20 mg dose), with adverse events similar to placebo throughout. The evidence is consistent but single-programme and Japan-only, matching the drug's Japan-only licence. This shelf is prophylaxis only; treatment is homed at pack #7208.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each trial's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: MVV (PARTIAL of #7067): means 150.6 L/min in Brazilian men and 103.4 in women; the FEV1 × 35–40 shortcut fails in Chinese adults (fitted multiplier ~45) and at 2,240 m, where ×35 underestimates by ~26% in men
shelves.question: In healthy adults, what is maximal voluntary ventilation — measured MVV in litres per minute and its prediction equations by age, sex and height — how well does the FEV1 × 35–40 shortcut approximate measured MVV, and how do values differ at altitude?
shelves.mesh: Humans · Male · Adult · Female · Brazil · Middle Aged · Respiratory Muscles · Aged · Muscle Strength · Reference Values · Maximal Voluntary Ventilation · Aged, 80 and over · Young Adult · Maximal Respiratory Pressures · Respiratory Function Tests · Forced Expiratory Volume · Altitude · Spirometry
shelves.balance: PARTIAL — home pack #7067. Pack #7067, read in full, asks maximal inspiratory / expiratory mouth pressures (MIP/MEP) and their weakness cut-offs; maximal voluntary ventilation is not its question, and this shelf cards only the MVV slice. One MVV dataset is already carded inside #7067 — Neder 1999 (PMID 10412550) — it is GATED for this shelf and is NOT re-carded here. Textbook framing: Boron & Boulpaep, respiratory mechanics / ventilatory capacity; Guyton & Hall, ch. 37. Four free datasets (Brazil 243; China 95; Mexico City at 2,240 m, 381; Madras 256) agree that MVV is strongly sex- and age-dependent and that the FEV1 × 35–40 shortcut fails outside its home population: in healthy Chinese adults the fitted multiplier was about 45, and at 2,240 m altitude MVV approached FEV1 × 45, with ×35 underestimating by about 26% in men. Manoeuvre duration (12 s extrapolated to a minute, where stated) is carded per study. PROPOSED STAMP: PHYSIOLOGY — EMERGING.

cards.headline: Brazilian reference values (Araújo 2024): 243 healthy adults — mean MVV 150.6 ± 35.2 L/min in men and 103.4 ± 23.2 L/min in women, with age-only prediction equations (men: 206.3 − 1.18 × age; women: 146.3 − 0.86 × age)
cards.summary: Brazilian reference values (Araújo 2024): 243 healthy adults — mean MVV 150.6 ± 35.2 L/min in men and 103.4 ± 23.2 L/min in women, with age-only prediction equations (men: 206.3 − 1.18 × age; women: 146.3 − 0.86 × age)
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (MVV reference values and prediction equations, multicentre Brazil) — PARTIAL slice: MVV limb only
cards.people: 243 healthy Brazilian adults (111 men, 132 women) aged 20–80 years assessed at three cities in the southeast and northeast of Brazil; this card reports only the maximal voluntary ventilation limb of a study that also measured MIP/MEP — those pressures are homed at pack #7067 and are not re-carded here.
cards.result: Mean MVV was higher in men (150.6 ± 35.2 L/min) than in women (103.4 ± 23.2 L/min) (P < 0.05). The proposed MVV prediction equations were: men, MVV = 206.3 − 1.18 × age (R² = 0.36, standard error of estimate 28.08); women, MVV = 146.3 − 0.86 × age (R² = 0.42, standard error of estimate 17.56). Age alone thus explains only about a third to two-fifths of MVV variance even in this healthy sample.
cards.watchOut: Age-only equations with R² of 0.36–0.42 and standard errors of 18–28 L/min are population descriptors, not precise individual predictions.
cards.source: Araújo PRS et al. Reference values for respiratory muscle strength and maximal voluntary ventilation in the Brazilian adult population: A multicentric study. PloS one. 2024. PMID: 39570848. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Chinese adults (Kor 2004): 95 healthy subjects — the fitted relation was MVV = FEV1 × 45.12 − 15.85, and the customary FEV1 × 35 and × 40 predictions were all significantly different from measured MVV (12-s manoeuvre)
cards.summary: Chinese adults (Kor 2004): 95 healthy subjects — the fitted relation was MVV = FEV1 × 45.12 − 15.85, and the customary FEV1 × 35 and × 40 predictions were all significantly different from measured MVV (12-s manoeuvre)
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (MVV prediction and FEV1-multiplier validity, healthy Chinese adults)
cards.people: 95 healthy Chinese adults (48 men, 47 women) recruited from the general population and stratified into five age groups from 20 to 70 years for both sexes; FEV1 and MVV measured with a clinical spirometer, MVV by the closed-circuit technique assessed for 12 s and calculated to L/min.
cards.result: Using FEV1 alone, the predictive equation obtained was MVV = FEV1 × 45.12 − 15.85 (adjusted r² = 0.792). Predicted MVV values using previously cited equations, including MVV = FEV1 × 35 or × 40, were all significantly different from the actual MVV values of these subjects. The authors conclude the previously cited FEV1-multiplier equations cannot be applied to healthy adult Chinese subjects.
cards.watchOut: A 12-s manoeuvre extrapolated to a minute, in 95 subjects from one population: the multiplier of about 45 is this sample's fit, not a new universal constant — that is exactly the shortcut's failure mode.
cards.source: Kor AC et al. Prediction of the maximal voluntary ventilation in healthy adult Chinese subjects. Respirology (Carlton, Vic.). 2004. PMID: 14982606. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Altitude 2,240 m (Cid-Juárez 2017): 381 residents of Mexico City — mean MVV 145.6 ± 48 L/min; FEV1 × 35 and × 40 both underestimated measured MVV (by about 26% in men and 10% in women), which approached FEV1 × 45
cards.summary: Altitude 2,240 m (Cid-Juárez 2017): 381 residents of Mexico City — mean MVV 145.6 ± 48 L/min; FEV1 × 35 and × 40 both underestimated measured MVV (by about 26% in men and 10% in women), which approached FEV1 × 45
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (measured MVV at altitude, Mexico City 2,240 m)
cards.people: 381 respiratory-healthy, non-obese volunteers older than 10 years (210 women, 55.1%; ages 10–80 years — the sample includes adolescents, printed here on the face) who had resided for more than 2 years in Mexico City at 2,240 m above sea level; forced spirometry and MVV performed to current standards.
cards.result: Mean MVV was 145.6 ± 48 L/min. Both FEV1 × 35 and FEV1 × 40 underestimated the observed MVV — in males by approximately 26% and in females by approximately 10%, as printed — and MVV for this population approached FEV1 × 45 (98 ± 15.6% of real MVV). Regression models including height, weight and measured FEV1 explained 70% of residual variability once sex was taken into account, with the best equations fitted separately by sex using age, age² and measured FEV1. The authors conclude sea-level reference values are inaccurate at this altitude, where reduced air density raises MVV relative to FEV1.
cards.watchOut: A convenience sample spanning ages 10–80, not an adults-only reference sample: its altitude lesson (the multiplier rises toward 45) is robust in direction, but its mean mixes adolescent and adult lungs.
cards.source: Cid-Juárez S et al. Maximum Voluntary Ventilation in a Population Residing at 2,240 Meters Above Sea Level. Respiratory care. 2017. PMID: 28830926. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Madras prediction equations (Vijayan 1993): 256 healthy non-smoking adults — mean MVV 126.7 ± 31.9 L/min in men and 77.7 ± 16.4 L/min in women, lower than Caucasian reports of the era
cards.summary: Madras prediction equations (Vijayan 1993): 256 healthy non-smoking adults — mean MVV 126.7 ± 31.9 L/min in men and 77.7 ± 16.4 L/min in women, lower than Caucasian reports of the era
cards.type: Primary human physiology study (MVV prediction equations, South Indian adults)
cards.people: 256 healthy non-smoking adults (132 men, 124 women) aged 15–63 years living in Madras, India; MVV measured and sex-specific regression equations derived for predicting MVV in South Indian adults. The fetched abstract is short (471 characters) but substantive, with values printed.
cards.result: Mean MVV (± SD) was 126.7 ± 31.9 L/min in men and 77.7 ± 16.4 L/min in women. MVV values in South Indians were similar to those reported for other Indian subjects, but lower than those reported for Caucasians — a further population offset of the kind the Brazilian, Chinese and altitude cards also show.
cards.watchOut: The short abstract prints means and the population comparison but not the equations themselves or the manoeuvre duration: no duration or equation is claimed from this card.
cards.source: Vijayan VK et al. Prediction equations for maximal voluntary ventilation in non-smoking normal subjects in Madras. Indian journal of physiology and pharmacology. 1993. PMID: 8225544. Framed by Boron & Boulpaep (respiratory mechanics / ventilatory capacity) and Guyton & Hall, ch. 37. Measured means: Brazil 150.6 ± 35.2 (men) and 103.4 ± 23.2 L/min (women) in 243 adults (Araújo 2024); Madras 126.7 ± 31.9 and 77.7 ± 16.4 L/min in 256 adults (Vijayan 1993); Mexico City at 2,240 m 145.6 ± 48 L/min across ages 10–80 (Cid-Juárez 2017). On the shortcut: Kor 2004 (95 Chinese adults, 12-s manoeuvre) fitted MVV = FEV1 × 45.12 − 15.85 and found ×35 and ×40 predictions all significantly wrong for that population, and Cid-Juárez found the same multipliers underestimating at altitude. PHYSIOLOGY — EMERGING: four concordant datasets totalling under 1,000 people, each bound to its population, altitude and manoeuvre duration, with no universal equation — the multiplier must be fitted, not assumed.
cards.watchOut: State the manoeuvre duration and the population whenever an MVV value or equation is used: a 12-s extrapolation in Chinese adults, an altitude sample including adolescents, and a sea-level Brazilian sample are three different measurements wearing one name.

shelves.title: Glycopyrronium monotherapy in COPD (GLOW programme): trough FEV1 ~100 mL above placebo, dyspnoea and health status improved, exacerbations down 31–34% in relative terms
shelves.question: In adults with moderate-to-severe COPD, does once-daily inhaled glycopyrronium bromide (50 µg, NVA237) versus placebo — or versus tiotropium — improve lung function, dyspnoea and exacerbations?
shelves.mesh: Female · Glycopyrrolate · Humans · Male · Muscarinic Antagonists · Pulmonary Disease, Chronic Obstructive · Quality of Life · Single-Blind Method · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: LIKELY benefit, from a single programme (GLOW) — two trials reported directly plus their pooled analysis, which is a programme report and not a third trial. Once-daily glycopyrronium bromide 50 µg (NVA237) improved trough FEV1 versus placebo by 108 mL at week 12 in GLOW1 (822 randomised) and by 97 mL in GLOW2 (1,066 randomised), with improved dyspnoea and health status and a 31% relative reduction in the risk of a first moderate/severe exacerbation in GLOW1 and 34% relative reduction in moderate-to-severe exacerbations in GLOW2 (both secondary endpoints; absolute exacerbation rates are not given in the fetched records). In GLOW2 glycopyrronium was comparable to open-label tiotropium on all outcomes. Primary endpoints are lung function at 12 weeks; the indacaterol–glycopyrronium combination and triple-therapy questions stay homed on their own shelves (live #1644, #1033) and are not re-carded here.

cards.headline: GLOW1 (D'Urzo 2011): glycopyrronium 50 µg once daily raised trough FEV1 by 108 mL versus placebo at week 12 and reduced the risk of a first moderate/severe exacerbation by 31% (relative reduction, P=0.023)
cards.summary: GLOW1 (D'Urzo 2011): glycopyrronium 50 µg once daily raised trough FEV1 by 108 mL versus placebo at week 12 and reduced the risk of a first moderate/severe exacerbation by 31% (relative reduction, P=0.023)
cards.type: Randomised trial (GLOW1), glycopyrronium (NVA237) 50 µg once daily vs placebo, 26 weeks
cards.people: 822 patients with moderate-to-severe COPD (smoking history ≥10 pack-years, post-bronchodilator FEV1 <80% and ≥30% predicted, FEV1/FVC <0.70) were randomised to NVA237 (glycopyrronium bromide) 50 µg once daily (n=552) or placebo (n=270) for 26 weeks; stabilised inhaled/intranasal corticosteroids or H1 antagonists were permitted.
cards.result: Trough FEV1 at week 12 was 1.408 ± 0.0105 L on NVA237 versus 1.301 ± 0.0137 L on placebo (treatment difference 108 ± 14.8 mL, P<0.001), with improvements from day 1 sustained to week 26. At week 26, transition dyspnoea index differed by 1.04 (P<0.001) and St George's Respiratory Questionnaire score by −2.81 (P=0.004) versus placebo. NVA237 reduced the risk of a first moderate/severe COPD exacerbation by 31% (relative reduction; P=0.023) and rescue-medication use by 0.46 puffs per day (P=0.005); cardiac and typical antimuscarinic adverse effects were infrequent.
cards.watchOut: The primary endpoint is a lung-function measure at 12 weeks; the exacerbation figure is a secondary endpoint expressed as a relative risk reduction, and the fetched record gives no absolute exacerbation rates.
cards.source: D'Urzo A et al. Efficacy and safety of once-daily NVA237 in patients with moderate-to-severe COPD: the GLOW1 trial. Respiratory research. 2011. PMID: 22151296. Registry ID: NCT01005901. cards.headline: GLOW2 (Kerwin 2012): over 52 weeks glycopyrronium raised trough FEV1 by 97 mL versus placebo at week 12, reduced moderate-to-severe exacerbations by 34% (relative reduction, P=0.001), and was comparable to open-label tiotropium
cards.summary: GLOW2 (Kerwin 2012): over 52 weeks glycopyrronium raised trough FEV1 by 97 mL versus placebo at week 12, reduced moderate-to-severe exacerbations by 34% (relative reduction, P=0.001), and was comparable to open-label tiotropium
cards.type: Randomised trial (GLOW2), glycopyrronium 50 µg once daily vs placebo and open-label tiotropium, 52 weeks
cards.people: 1,066 patients with moderate-to-severe COPD were randomised 2:1:1 to NVA237 (glycopyrronium) 50 µg once daily, placebo, or open-label tiotropium 18 µg once daily for 52 weeks; 810 patients completed the study.
cards.result: At week 12 trough FEV1 increased by 97 mL with NVA237 versus placebo (95% CI 64.6 to 130.2; P<0.001) and by 83 mL with tiotropium (95% CI 45.6 to 121.4; P<0.001). NVA237 improved dyspnoea (transition dyspnoea index at week 26, P=0.002) and health status (St George's Respiratory Questionnaire at week 52, P<0.001) versus placebo, reduced the risk of moderate-to-severe exacerbations by 34% (relative reduction; P=0.001) and rescue-medication use (P=0.039); NVA237–placebo and tiotropium–placebo differences were comparable for all outcomes, and safety profiles were similar across groups.
cards.watchOut: The tiotropium arm was open-label, and the exacerbation claim rests on secondary endpoints expressed as relative reductions without absolute rates in the fetched record; a quarter of randomised patients did not complete the study.
cards.source: Kerwin E et al. Efficacy and safety of NVA237 versus placebo and tiotropium in patients with COPD: the GLOW2 study. The European respiratory journal. 2012. PMID: 23060624. cards.headline: Pooled GLOW1/GLOW2 analysis (D'Urzo 2014) — programme report, not a third trial: pooled trough FEV1 difference 103 mL at week 12, with time to first moderate/severe exacerbation prolonged by 36% (relative) over 26 weeks and 33% over 52 weeks
cards.summary: Pooled GLOW1/GLOW2 analysis (D'Urzo 2014) — programme report, not a third trial: pooled trough FEV1 difference 103 mL at week 12, with time to first moderate/severe exacerbation prolonged by 36% (relative) over 26 weeks and 33% over 52 weeks
cards.type: Programme report: post-hoc pooled analysis of the GLOW1 and GLOW2 trials (same programme as the two cards above — not an independent third trial)
cards.people: Post-hoc pooled analysis of GLOW1 and GLOW2: 1,888 subjects randomised, 98.2% analysed (glycopyrronium 1,059, tiotropium 267, placebo 528); serial 24-hour spirometry was performed in a subset.
cards.result: Pooled least-squares mean trough FEV1 at week 12 was higher with glycopyrronium than placebo by 103 ± 11.2 mL (P<0.001), with significant differences also at day 1 and weeks 26 and 52; glycopyrronium improved FEV1 within 5–15 minutes of the first dose versus both placebo and tiotropium. Time to first moderate or severe exacerbation was significantly prolonged versus placebo over 26 and 52 weeks (36% and 33% relative prolongations as reported; both P<0.001), and dyspnoea, health status and rescue-medication use all favoured glycopyrronium, which was safe and well tolerated.
cards.watchOut: A pooled re-analysis of the two trials carded above: it adds precision and 24-hour spirometry detail but no new patients, and must not be counted as a third trial.
cards.source: D'Urzo A et al. Once daily glycopyrronium for the treatment of COPD: pooled analysis of the GLOW1 and GLOW2 studies. Current medical research and opinion. 2014. PMID: 24156566. shelves.title: Olodaterol monotherapy in COPD: FEV1 improved vs placebo in two replicate 48-week trials (one publication); one-year pooled safety comparable to placebo; licensed dose 5 µg
shelves.question: In adults with GOLD 2–4 COPD, does once-daily olodaterol (5 or 10 µg via Respimat) versus placebo improve lung function over 48 weeks, and how does it compare with its fixed-dose partner tiotropium as a mono-component?
shelves.mesh: Administration, Inhalation · Adrenergic beta-2 Receptor Agonists · Aged · Area Under Curve · Asia · Australia · Benzoxazines · Bronchodilator Agents · Double-Blind Method · Equipment Design · Female · Forced Expiratory Volume · Germany · Humans · Lung · Male · Middle Aged · Nebulizers and Vaporizers · New Zealand · Predictive Value of Tests · Pulmonary Disease, Chronic Obstructive · Severity of Illness Index · Time Factors · Treatment Outcome · United States
shelves.balance: LIKELY benefit for lung function, from a single programme. The floor of this shelf is three reports: two replicate 48-week trials published as ONE publication, a mono-component comparison from the tiotropium/olodaterol combination programme (TONADO), and a pre-specified pooled one-year safety analysis — stated plainly so the replicate trials are never double-counted. Olodaterol 5 µg and 10 µg once daily via Respimat significantly improved FEV1 AUC0–3 and trough FEV1 versus placebo at week 12 in both replicate trials (624 and 642 patients evaluated), on top of usual-care background therapy. The licensed dose is 5 µg; the 10 µg arm is a trial dose and is labelled as such wherever it appears. In TONADO, the fixed-dose combination beat its mono-components — that comparison is carded for what it shows about the olodaterol component, not as combination evidence. Pooled safety over 48 weeks (3,104 patients) was comparable to placebo and formoterol.

cards.headline: Replicate 48-week trials 1222.11/1222.12 (Ferguson 2014) — two trials in ONE publication: olodaterol 5 µg and 10 µg both significantly improved FEV1 AUC0–3 and trough FEV1 versus placebo at week 12
cards.summary: Replicate 48-week trials 1222.11/1222.12 (Ferguson 2014) — two trials in ONE publication: olodaterol 5 µg and 10 µg both significantly improved FEV1 AUC0–3 and trough FEV1 versus placebo at week 12
cards.type: Two replicate phase III randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trials reported in one publication, olodaterol 5/10 µg once daily vs placebo, 48 weeks (counts as one publication)
cards.people: 624 patients (study 1222.11) and 642 patients (study 1222.12) with moderate-to-very-severe (GOLD 2–4) COPD were evaluated in two replicate randomised double-blind placebo-controlled phase III trials of olodaterol 5 µg or 10 µg or placebo once daily via Respimat for 48 weeks, with usual-care background therapy continued.
cards.result: In both studies, olodaterol 5 µg and 10 µg significantly improved the co-primary endpoints at week 12: FEV1 AUC0–3 response (P<0.0001 in both studies) and trough FEV1 response (study 1222.11, P<0.0001; study 1222.12, P<0.05 on post-hoc testing). Secondary endpoints — further lung-function measures, rescue-medication use, FEV1 AUC0–12 and Patient Global Rating over 48 weeks — supported the efficacy of olodaterol, and adverse-event incidence was comparable with placebo.
cards.watchOut: Two trials but one publication — counted once on this shelf. Endpoints are lung function; the 10 µg arm is a trial dose (the licensed dose is 5 µg), one trough-FEV1 result rests on post-hoc testing, and patients continued usual-care background therapy, so this is not a pure no-treatment comparison.
cards.source: Ferguson GT et al. Efficacy and safety of olodaterol once daily delivered via Respimat® in patients with GOLD 2-4 COPD: results from two replicate 48-week studies. cards.type: Two replicate phase III randomised double-blind trials (TONADO), fixed-dose tiotropium/olodaterol vs mono-components — carded for its olodaterol mono-component limb, as the commissioning row directs
cards.people: 5,162 patients with moderate-to-very-severe COPD received treatment in two replicate randomised double-blind phase III trials (2,624 in study 1237.5 and 2,538 in study 1237.6): tiotropium + olodaterol fixed-dose combination 2.5/5 µg or 5/5 µg, tiotropium 2.5 µg or 5 µg, or olodaterol 5 µg, all once daily via Respimat for 52 weeks.
cards.result: Both fixed-dose combinations significantly improved FEV1 AUC0–3 and trough FEV1 responses versus the mono-components (including olodaterol 5 µg alone) in both studies at week 24; St George's Respiratory Questionnaire total score improved significantly versus the mono-components only for the 5/5 µg combination. Adverse-event incidence was comparable between the combinations and the mono-components.
cards.watchOut: This is a combination-programme trial: it shows the combination beat olodaterol alone on lung function, and it contains no placebo arm, so it cannot by itself establish olodaterol monotherapy efficacy — that rests on the placebo-controlled replicate trials above. The tiotropium/olodaterol combination question itself stays homed on its own shelf.
cards.source: Buhl R et al. Tiotropium and olodaterol fixed-dose combination versus mono-components in COPD (GOLD 2-4). The European respiratory journal. 2015. PMID: 25573406. Registry ID: NCT01431274; NCT01431287. cards.headline: Pooled one-year safety analysis (McGarvey 2015): in 3,104 patients, adverse events (71.2%), serious adverse events (16.1%) and deaths (1.7%) were balanced across olodaterol, placebo and formoterol groups
cards.summary: Pooled one-year safety analysis (McGarvey 2015): in 3,104 patients, adverse events (71.2%), serious adverse events (16.1%) and deaths (1.7%) were balanced across olodaterol, placebo and formoterol groups
cards.type: Pre-specified pooled safety analysis of four phase III randomised trials (programme report of the olodaterol programme, including the replicate trials carded above)
cards.people: Pre-specified pooled analysis of four randomised double-blind placebo-controlled phase III studies (1222.11–1222.14) in GOLD 2–4 COPD: 3,104 patients in the safety analysis — olodaterol 5 µg (n=876), olodaterol 10 µg (n=883), placebo (n=885) and formoterol 12 µg twice daily (n=460) — treated for 48 weeks on background maintenance therapy; about 60% received concomitant cardiovascular therapy and 25% had a history of cardiac disease.
cards.result: Overall on-treatment adverse events (71.2%), serious adverse events (16.1%) and deaths (1.7%) were balanced across treatment groups; respiratory and cardiovascular adverse events, including major adverse cardiac events, occurred at similar frequencies on placebo and active treatments, with in-depth ECG and Holter monitoring. The authors concluded the safety profiles of olodaterol 5 µg (the marketed, registered dose) and 10 µg were comparable to placebo and formoterol, with no safety signals identified.
cards.watchOut: A pooled safety analysis of the same programme — it overlaps the replicate efficacy trials and adds the two 1222.13/1222.14 studies; it is a safety report, not independent efficacy evidence. The 10 µg dose is a trial dose; 5 µg is the marketed dose.
cards.source: McGarvey L et al. One-Year Safety of Olodaterol Once Daily via Respimat® in Patients with GOLD 2-4 Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease: Results of a Pre-Specified Pooled Analysis. COPD. 2015. PMID: 25692310. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: olodaterol 5 µg once daily improves lung function versus placebo over 48 weeks in two replicate trials (one publication), the TONADO programme shows the fixed-dose combination beats the olodaterol mono-component, and pooled one-year safety in 3,104 patients is comparable to placebo and formoterol
cards.summary: Synthesis: olodaterol 5 µg once daily improves lung function versus placebo over 48 weeks in two replicate trials (one publication), the TONADO programme shows the fixed-dose combination beats the olodaterol mono-component, and pooled one-year safety in 3,104 patients is comparable to placebo and formoterol
cards.type: Synthesis
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: The monotherapy efficacy read rests on the replicate placebo-controlled trials (624 and 642 patients evaluated), which agree on significant FEV1 AUC0–3 and trough FEV1 improvements at week 12 sustained over 48 weeks. TONADO contributes the mono-component comparison (combination superior to olodaterol alone on lung function) and the pooled analysis contributes one-year safety. No exacerbation-outcome or mortality trial of olodaterol monotherapy is carded; endpoints are lung function and safety, and the 10 µg arm is a trial dose above the licensed 5 µg.

shelves.title: Indacaterol monotherapy in COPD: trough FEV1 170–180 mL above placebo across three trials, ahead of salmeterol and formoterol; no exacerbation-outcome trial exists
shelves.question: In adults with moderate-to-severe COPD, does once-daily indacaterol (150 or 300 µg) versus placebo — or versus tiotropium, salmeterol or formoterol — improve lung function and symptoms?
shelves.mesh: Administration, Inhalation · Blood Glucose · Bronchodilator Agents · Double-Blind Method · Drug Administration Schedule · Dyspnea · Electrocardiography · Female · Forced Expiratory Volume · Health Status · Humans · Indans · Male · Middle Aged · Potassium · Pulmonary Disease, Chronic Obstructive · Quinolones · Scopolamine Derivatives · Spirometry · Tiotropium Bromide
shelves.balance: LIKELY benefit for lung function and symptoms, from a 2010–2011 programme with lung-function and symptom endpoints — no exacerbation-outcome or mortality trial of indacaterol monotherapy exists, and that absence is stated on the face. Once-daily indacaterol raised trough FEV1 versus placebo by 180 mL at week 12 in INHANCE (1,683 randomised; both 150 and 300 µg), by 170 mL versus placebo and 60 mL versus twice-daily salmeterol in INLIGHT-2 (1,002 randomised), and by 170 mL versus placebo and 100 mL versus twice-daily formoterol in the one-year Dahl trial (1,732 randomised), with dyspnoea and health-status improvements. The tiotropium arm of INHANCE was open-label — stated on its card. This is one of three separate once-daily bronchodilator monotherapy shelves (with glycopyrronium, #7347, and olodaterol, #7348); the indacaterol–glycopyrronium combination and triple-therapy questions stay homed elsewhere (live #1644, #1033).

cards.headline: INHANCE (Donohue 2010): indacaterol 150 and 300 µg raised trough FEV1 by 180 mL versus placebo at week 12 (tiotropium by 140 mL); dyspnoea and health status also improved over 26 weeks
cards.summary: INHANCE (Donohue 2010): indacaterol 150 and 300 µg raised trough FEV1 by 180 mL versus placebo at week 12 (tiotropium by 140 mL); dyspnoea and health status also improved over 26 weeks
cards.type: Randomised trial (INHANCE), double-blind indacaterol vs placebo with an open-label tiotropium arm, 26 weeks
cards.people: 1,683 patients with moderate-to-severe COPD (mean age 63.3 years, post-bronchodilator FEV1 56% predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.53) were randomised to double-blind indacaterol 150 µg or 300 µg or placebo, or open-label tiotropium 18 µg, all once daily for 26 weeks.
cards.result: Trough FEV1 at week 12 rose versus placebo by 180 mL with both indacaterol doses and by 140 mL with tiotropium (all P<0.001 versus placebo). At week 26, versus placebo, transition dyspnoea index increased by 1.00 (150 µg) and 1.18 (300 µg) (P<0.001) and St George's Respiratory Questionnaire total score fell by −3.3 and −2.4 (P<0.01); tiotropium's corresponding results were 0.87 (P<0.001) and −1.0 (not significant). Adverse events, low serum potassium, high blood glucose and prolonged QTc occurred at similar rates across treatments.
cards.watchOut: The tiotropium arm was OPEN-LABEL, so indacaterol–tiotropium comparisons carry performance and reporting bias risk; the primary endpoint is lung function at 12 weeks, and additional analyses were not adjusted for multiplicity.
cards.source: Donohue JF et al. Once-daily bronchodilators for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: indacaterol versus tiotropium. American journal of respiratory and critical care medicine. 2010. PMID: 20463178. Registry ID: NCT00463567. cards.headline: INLIGHT-2 (Kornmann 2011): indacaterol 150 µg raised trough FEV1 by 170 mL versus placebo and 60 mL versus twice-daily salmeterol at week 12
cards.summary: INLIGHT-2 (Kornmann 2011): indacaterol 150 µg raised trough FEV1 by 170 mL versus placebo and 60 mL versus twice-daily salmeterol at week 12
cards.type: Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial (INLIGHT-2), indacaterol once daily vs salmeterol twice daily vs placebo, 6 months
cards.people: 1,002 patients with moderate-to-severe COPD were randomised to 6 months of double-blind indacaterol 150 µg once daily, salmeterol 50 µg twice daily or placebo; 838 (84%) completed the study.
cards.result: Indacaterol increased trough FEV1 at week 12 by 170 mL over placebo (P<0.001) and by 60 mL over salmeterol (P<0.001). Both active treatments improved health status (St George's Respiratory Questionnaire) and dyspnoea (transition dyspnoea index) versus placebo, with differences between the active treatments favouring indacaterol. Safety profiles were similar across groups and both active treatments were well tolerated.
cards.watchOut: Lung-function primary endpoint at 12 weeks in a 2010–2011 programme; 16% of randomised patients did not complete, and there is no exacerbation-outcome or mortality endpoint.
cards.source: Kornmann O et al. Once-daily indacaterol versus twice-daily salmeterol for COPD: a placebo-controlled comparison. The European respiratory journal. 2011. PMID: 20693243. cards.headline: Indacaterol versus formoterol (Dahl 2010): over 52 weeks indacaterol raised 24-hour post-dose FEV1 by 170 mL versus placebo and 100 mL versus twice-daily formoterol at week 12, maintained at week 52
cards.summary: Indacaterol versus formoterol (Dahl 2010): over 52 weeks indacaterol raised 24-hour post-dose FEV1 by 170 mL versus placebo and 100 mL versus twice-daily formoterol at week 12, maintained at week 52
cards.type: Randomised double-blind double-dummy trial, indacaterol once daily vs formoterol twice daily vs placebo, 52 weeks
cards.people: 1,732 patients with moderate-to-severe COPD were randomised to once-daily indacaterol 300 µg (n=437) or 600 µg (n=428), twice-daily formoterol 12 µg (n=435) or placebo (n=432) for 52 weeks in a double-blind double-dummy parallel-group study.
cards.result: Indacaterol increased 24-hour post-dose FEV1 after 12 weeks by 170 mL (both doses) versus placebo and by 100 mL versus formoterol (all P<0.001), with the differences maintained at 52 weeks. Symptomatic outcomes improved versus placebo with all active treatments; indacaterol was more effective than formoterol on transition dyspnoea index and need for as-needed salbutamol. Indacaterol was well tolerated with minimal impact on QTc interval and systemic beta-2-mediated events.
cards.watchOut: The indacaterol doses tested (300 and 600 µg) are above the 150 µg dose used in INHANCE and INLIGHT-2; endpoints are lung function, symptoms and health status — exacerbations were recorded but this is not an exacerbation-outcome or mortality trial.
cards.source: Dahl R et al. Efficacy of a new once-daily long-acting inhaled beta2-agonist indacaterol versus twice-daily formoterol in COPD. Thorax. 2010. PMID: 20522841. Registry ID: NCT00393458. shelves.title: Arformoterol (nebulised) in COPD: trough FEV1 beat placebo across four 12-week trials in three reports; one open-label year shows no tolerance, more tremor than salmeterol
shelves.question: In adults with moderate-to-severe COPD, does twice-daily nebulised arformoterol (the (R,R)-enantiomer of formoterol) versus placebo — or versus salmeterol/formoterol — improve airway function, and is long-term use safe?
shelves.mesh: Administration, Inhalation · Bronchoconstriction · Bronchodilator Agents · Double-Blind Method · Ethanolamines · Female · Follow-Up Studies · Forced Expiratory Volume · Formoterol Fumarate · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Nebulizers and Vaporizers · Pulmonary Disease, Chronic Obstructive · Single-Blind Method · Treatment Outcome
shelves.balance: LIKELY benefit for airway function, with one-year safety data. Arformoterol is the (R,R)-enantiomer of formoterol given as a nebulised solution (marketed as Brovana — the specific tested product, named under the clarification exception because the nebulised delivery is the point of the question). The floor is three reports covering at least four trials: two 12-week trials pooled in one publication (1,456 subjects), a separate 12-week placebo- and active-controlled trial (717 patients), and a one-year open-label safety comparison against salmeterol (793 treated) — the two-trials-one-publication report counts as one publication, stated on the face. Nebulised arformoterol improved trough FEV1 versus placebo by 10.9–15.4 percentage points across doses over 12 weeks, improved dyspnoea versus placebo where salmeterol did not reach significance, and over one year showed no increase in exacerbation frequency and no clinically meaningful tolerance; tremor was more frequent than with salmeterol (13.4% vs 1.1%). Endpoints are airway function and safety/tolerance, not exacerbations or mortality.

cards.headline: Two trials, one publication (Hanrahan 2008): nebulised arformoterol improved trough FEV1 versus placebo by 11.4 (15 µg twice daily), 15.4 (25 µg twice daily) and 10.9 (50 µg once daily) percentage points averaged over 12 weeks
cards.summary: Two trials, one publication (Hanrahan 2008): nebulised arformoterol improved trough FEV1 versus placebo by 11.4 (15 µg twice daily), 15.4 (25 µg twice daily) and 10.9 (50 µg once daily) percentage points averaged over 12 weeks
cards.type: Two identical 12-week double-blind randomised trials reported and pooled in one publication, nebulised arformoterol vs salmeterol vs placebo (counts as one publication)
cards.people: 1,456 subjects with COPD (mean FEV1 1.2 L, 41% predicted) across two identical 12-week double-blind randomised trials of nebulised arformoterol 15 µg twice daily, 25 µg twice daily or 50 µg once daily, salmeterol metered-dose inhaler 42 µg twice daily, or placebo; data were pooled.
cards.result: Improvement in trough FEV1 averaged over 12 weeks was greater for arformoterol and salmeterol than placebo (mean differences from placebo: arformoterol 15 µg twice daily 11.4% [95% CI 8.4 to 14.3], 25 µg twice daily 15.4% [12.2 to 18.6], 50 µg once daily 10.9% [7.9 to 13.9]; salmeterol 11.6% [8.8 to 14.4]). Improvements were present after the first dose and at week 12, with all 95% CIs excluding zero; FEV1 AUC0–12 and peak percent change were greater for arformoterol than salmeterol. After 12 weeks, 78–87% of arformoterol subjects had ≥10% FEV1 increases from pre-dose (56% salmeterol, 44% placebo), with median time to response 3–13 minutes versus 142 minutes for salmeterol.
cards.watchOut: Two trials in one publication — counted once on this shelf; results are percentage changes in lung function over 12 weeks, not exacerbation or mortality outcomes, and the pooled report does not give per-trial results.
cards.source: Hanrahan JP et al. Effect of nebulized arformoterol on airway function in COPD: results from two randomized trials. COPD. 2008. PMID: 18259972. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Baumgartner 2007: in 717 patients, all arformoterol doses beat placebo on trough FEV1 over 12 weeks (+14.9% to +18.9% vs +6.0%) and on dyspnoea, where salmeterol's dyspnoea difference was not significant
cards.summary: Baumgartner 2007: in 717 patients, all arformoterol doses beat placebo on trough FEV1 over 12 weeks (+14.9% to +18.9% vs +6.0%) and on dyspnoea, where salmeterol's dyspnoea difference was not significant
cards.type: 12-week multicentre randomised double-blind double-dummy placebo- and active-controlled trial, nebulised arformoterol vs salmeterol vs placebo
cards.people: 717 patients aged ≥35 years with physician-diagnosed COPD at 60 US centres (mean age 62.9 years, 58% men, mean baseline FEV1 1.2 L, 41% predicted) received arformoterol 15 µg twice daily, 25 µg twice daily or 50 µg once daily by nebuliser, salmeterol 42 µg twice daily by metered-dose inhaler, or placebo for 12 weeks in this double-blind double-dummy trial.
cards.result: Mean improvement in trough FEV1 over 12 weeks was significantly greater with all three arformoterol doses (15 µg twice daily +16.9%, 25 µg twice daily +18.9%, 50 µg once daily +14.9%) and with salmeterol (+17.4%) than placebo (+6.0%; P<0.001). FEV1 AUC0–12 percentage change also favoured all arformoterol doses over placebo and over salmeterol (P≤0.024). Transition dyspnoea index focal scores at week 12 were significantly greater than placebo for all arformoterol doses (0.97 to 1.08) but not for salmeterol (0.36; 95% CI −0.40 to 1.12). Health-status (SGRQ) differences versus placebo suggested significant improvement only for arformoterol 25 µg twice daily and salmeterol. Adverse events and COPD exacerbations occurred at similar frequency across all groups including placebo.
cards.watchOut: Lung-function and symptom endpoints over 12 weeks in patients with quite severe airflow limitation (mean FEV1 41% predicted); three arformoterol dose regimens were tested, of which 15 µg twice daily is the marketed regimen.
cards.source: Baumgartner RA et al. Nebulized arformoterol in patients with COPD: a 12-week, multicenter, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, placebo- and active-controlled trial. Clinical therapeutics. 2007. PMID: 17472819. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: One-year safety evaluation (Donohue 2008) — OPEN-LABEL: arformoterol 50 µg once daily and salmeterol were both well tolerated over 12 months, exacerbation frequency did not rise, and no clinically meaningful tolerance developed; tremor was more frequent on arformoterol (13.4% vs 1.1%)
cards.summary: One-year safety evaluation (Donohue 2008) — OPEN-LABEL: arformoterol 50 µg once daily and salmeterol were both well tolerated over 12 months, exacerbation frequency did not rise, and no clinically meaningful tolerance developed; tremor was more frequent on arformoterol (13.4% vs 1.1%)
cards.type: Prospective multicentre OPEN-LABEL 12-month safety and tolerance trial, nebulised arformoterol vs salmeterol (no placebo arm)
cards.people: 793 subjects with COPD (mean FEV1 1.2 L, ~41% predicted) were treated in this prospective multicentre open-label 12-month trial: nebulised arformoterol 50 µg once daily (n=528) or salmeterol 42 µg twice daily by metered-dose inhaler (n=265).
cards.result: Adverse-event frequency was similar (arformoterol 90.5%, salmeterol 88.3%), but tremor was more frequent on arformoterol (13.4% vs 1.1%). COPD exacerbation frequency did not increase over 12 months (weeks 0–13: 15.7% arformoterol, 11.7% salmeterol; weeks 39–52: 10.0% and 9.4%). Rescue ipratropium and albuterol use fell by 0.8 to 1.5 actuations/day in both groups and stayed down. Mean trough FEV1 improved at week 13 (7.1% ± 17.0 arformoterol, 7.6% ± 17.8 salmeterol) and the improvement continued at week 52 (5.9% and 6.2%); mean peak post-dose FEV1 declined by about 2% over the year in both groups.
cards.watchOut: Open-label with no placebo arm and a higher arformoterol dose (50 µg once daily) than the marketed 15 µg twice-daily regimen: it answers long-term safety and tolerance questions, not efficacy, and the tremor difference (13.4% vs 1.1%) is its clearest comparative signal.
cards.source: Donohue JF et al. Arformoterol and salmeterol in the treatment of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a one year evaluation of safety and tolerance. Therapeutic advances in respiratory disease. 2008. PMID: 19124357. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Synthesis: nebulised arformoterol improves airway function versus placebo over 12 weeks in at least four trials reported in three publications (1,456 pooled subjects; 717 patients), and one open-label year of use shows no rising exacerbation frequency and no meaningful tolerance, at the cost of more tremor than salmeterol
cards.summary: Synthesis: nebulised arformoterol improves airway function versus placebo over 12 weeks in at least four trials reported in three publications (1,456 pooled subjects; 717 patients), and one open-label year of use shows no rising exacerbation frequency and no meaningful tolerance, at the cost of more tremor than salmeterol
cards.type: Synthesis
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: The 12-week placebo-controlled evidence is consistent across doses (trough FEV1 advantages of roughly 11–15 percentage points in the pooled two-trial report; +14.9% to +18.9% versus +6.0% on placebo in the Baumgartner trial), with dyspnoea benefits versus placebo. The one-year report is open-label and safety-focused. No trial tests exacerbations or mortality as outcomes, and the delivery route — a nebulised single-enantiomer solution (Brovana) — is itself the clinical point of this question, distinct from inhaler formoterol/salmeterol questions homed elsewhere.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each report's limits; this synthesis adds no new data.
cards.source: Synthesis of the reports carded above; no additional source.

shelves.title: Nedocromil sodium in chronic asthma: modest symptom and peak-flow benefits in four small 1988–1996 trials; the steroid-resistant trial had N=12 completers and is never load-bearing
shelves.question: In adults with chronic asthma — including asthma dependent on inhaled corticosteroids and steroid-resistant asthma — does inhaled nedocromil sodium versus placebo improve symptoms and lung function and spare corticosteroids?
shelves.mesh: Adolescent · Adrenal Cortex Hormones · Adult · Aged · Anti-Inflammatory Agents, Non-Steroidal · Asthma · Double-Blind Method · Female · Humans · Male · Middle Aged · Nedocromil · Quinolones · Randomized Controlled Trials as Topic · Respiratory Function Tests
shelves.balance: POSSIBLE benefit — modest, on small, old evidence, and the era is printed on the face: every trial is from 1988–1996, short (4 weeks to 3 months), with symptom and lung-function endpoints and no exacerbation-outcome trial. Inhaled nedocromil sodium 4 mg four times daily (twice daily in one trial) added to existing therapy gave small but significant advantages over placebo in inhaled-corticosteroid-dependent asthma (89 and 188 patients), in a 30-patient bronchodilator-maintained trial, and in steroid-resistant asthma — that last trial is very small (26 randomised; N=12 nedocromil patients completed treatment) and is never load-bearing on this shelf. Nedocromil was withdrawn from several markets for commercial (not safety) reasons. Sodium cromoglicate does not join this shelf — its adult base did not verify at floor, as the commissioning row records.

cards.headline: Bone 1989: in inhaled-corticosteroid-dependent asthma, nedocromil added after steroid dose reduction beat placebo on diary peak flow (mean difference 18 L/min), daytime asthma score (0.42) and night bronchodilator use over 4 weeks
cards.summary: Bone 1989: in inhaled-corticosteroid-dependent asthma, nedocromil added after steroid dose reduction beat placebo on diary peak flow (mean difference 18 L/min), daytime asthma score (0.42) and night bronchodilator use over 4 weeks
cards.type: Double-blind randomised placebo-controlled trial, nedocromil added in inhaled-corticosteroid-dependent asthma after steroid reduction, 4 weeks
cards.people: 89 adults with asthma receiving inhaled corticosteroid and bronchodilator treatment took part in this double-blind randomised placebo-controlled trial of nedocromil sodium 4 mg four times daily by inhalation; during a 2–4-week run-in, corticosteroid dose was reduced where possible to produce comparable symptoms across the population, and test treatment lasted 4 weeks.
cards.result: Symptoms improved more on nedocromil than placebo, with significant differences for diary-card peak expiratory flow readings, asthma symptom scores and night-time bronchodilator usage. The mean between-group differences were 18 L/min for peak flow, 0.42 for daytime asthma score, and 1.73 puffs in 24 hours for bronchodilator usage.
cards.watchOut: A 1989 trial with a 4-week treatment period after a deliberate steroid-reduction run-in: the effects are small diary-card differences, and the design tests nedocromil as a steroid-sparing add-on, not as a replacement for inhaled corticosteroids.
cards.source: Bone MF et al. Nedocromil sodium in adults with asthma dependent on inhaled corticosteroids: a double blind, placebo controlled study. Thorax. 1989. PMID: 2552600. cards.headline: Canadian multicentre trial (Rebuck 1990): in steroid-dependent asthma, 12 weeks of nedocromil gave slight but significant benefit over placebo in symptom scores, peak flow and inhaled beta-agonist use (127 on nedocromil, 61 on placebo)
cards.summary: Canadian multicentre trial (Rebuck 1990): in steroid-dependent asthma, 12 weeks of nedocromil gave slight but significant benefit over placebo in symptom scores, peak flow and inhaled beta-agonist use (127 on nedocromil, 61 on placebo)
cards.type: Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled multicentre trial, nedocromil added to established therapy in steroid-dependent asthma, 12 weeks
cards.people: 188 patients with steroid-dependent asthma on established regimens including steroids and bronchodilators received nedocromil sodium (n=127) or placebo (n=61), two puffs of 2 mg four times daily, for 12 weeks in this double-blind group-comparative Canadian multicentre study.
cards.result: Diary-card symptom scores, morning and evening peak expiratory flow values and inhaled beta-agonist usage all showed slight but significant benefit from adding nedocromil sodium. Ten patients developed adverse reactions (seven on active drug, three on placebo), and two patients in each group withdrew because of worsening asthma. The authors concluded nedocromil could be added to asthma regimens with a reasonable expectation of further modest symptomatic benefit.
cards.watchOut: A 1990 trial whose own wording is 'slight' and 'modest' benefit on diary measures; unequal group sizes (127 vs 61), and no exacerbation or steroid-dose outcome is reported in the fetched record.

cards.headline: Fairfax 1988: in 30 bronchodilator-maintained asthmatic patients, nedocromil 4 mg twice daily beat placebo on night-time and daytime asthma, cough, daytime bronchodilator use and clinic FEV1 by week 4
cards.summary: Fairfax 1988: in 30 bronchodilator-maintained asthmatic patients, nedocromil 4 mg twice daily beat placebo on night-time and daytime asthma, cough, daytime bronchodilator use and clinic FEV1 by week 4
cards.type: Double-blind group comparative randomised trial, nedocromil vs placebo on bronchodilator therapy, 3 months
cards.people: 30 adult asthmatic patients maintained on bronchodilator therapy were randomised, 15 to nedocromil sodium 4 mg twice daily and 15 to placebo, for 3 months in this double-blind group comparative trial.
cards.result: Significant differences in favour of nedocromil were observed by week 4 for night-time asthma, daytime asthma, cough, daytime bronchodilator use and clinic assessment of forced expiratory volume in 1 second. Diurnal variation in peak expiratory flow was reduced on nedocromil. There were no serious adverse reactions and no treatment-related changes in haematology, blood biochemistry or urinalysis.
cards.watchOut: The smallest of the main trials (n=30, 15 per arm) and the oldest (1988), using a twice-daily regimen rather than the four-times-daily dosing of the other trials; symptom and lung-function endpoints only.
cards.source: Fairfax AJ et al. A double-blind group comparative trial of nedocromil sodium and placebo in the management of bronchial asthma. The Journal of international medical research. 1988. cards.headline: Steroid-resistant asthma RCT (Marin 1996) — very small, N printed on the face and never load-bearing: 26 patients randomised (13 nedocromil, 13 placebo), N=12 nedocromil patients completed; FEV1 rose 11.4% on nedocromil at 12 weeks (P=0.05)
cards.summary: Steroid-resistant asthma RCT (Marin 1996) — very small, N printed on the face and never load-bearing: 26 patients randomised (13 nedocromil, 13 placebo), N=12 nedocromil patients completed; FEV1 rose 11.4% on nedocromil at 12 weeks (P=0.05)
cards.type: Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial in steroid-resistant asthma — very small (26 randomised; N=12 completed on nedocromil), carded for completeness and never load-bearing
cards.people: Patients with steroid-resistant asthma — defined as ≥20% FEV1 improvement after inhaled salbutamol but failure of FEV1 to improve by at least 15% after a 2-week trial of prednisolone 30 mg daily — were randomised double-blind to inhaled nedocromil sodium 4 mg four times daily (n=13) or placebo (n=13) for 3 months; 12 nedocromil patients completed the treatment period.
cards.result: Nedocromil, but not placebo, produced a mean FEV1 increase of 11.4% after 12 weeks (P=0.05), morning peak-flow increases of 12.4% (P=0.04) at 8 weeks and 15% (P=0.02) at 12 weeks, reduced peak-flow variability (P=0.02) and salbutamol use (P=0.005), and improved quality of life (P=0.007) by trial end. Six of the 12 nedocromil patients who completed treatment showed a 'good response' (salbutamol use down >50% and morning peak flow up >20%), with no baseline predictors of response. Two patients withdrew with severe exacerbation, one from each group.
cards.watchOut: N=12 nedocromil completers: this trial is printed with its N on the face, is the only evidence in the specific steroid-resistant population, and is never load-bearing for this shelf's stamp — the shelf rests on the three larger (though still small and old) trials above. Response was heterogeneous — half the completers met the 'good response' definition and half did not.
cards.source: Marin JM et al. Effects of nedocromil sodium in steroid-resistant asthma: a randomized controlled trial. The Journal of allergy and clinical immunology. 1996. PMID: 8621845. cards.headline: Synthesis: four 1988–1996 placebo-controlled trials (89, 188, 30 and 26 randomised) consistently show small symptomatic and peak-flow benefits from adding inhaled nedocromil in chronic asthma, including steroid-dependent asthma — old, short, modest evidence with no exacerbation-outcome trial
cards.summary: Synthesis: four 1988–1996 placebo-controlled trials (89, 188, 30 and 26 randomised) consistently show small symptomatic and peak-flow benefits from adding inhaled nedocromil in chronic asthma, including steroid-dependent asthma — old, short, modest evidence with no exacerbation-outcome trial
cards.type: Synthesis
cards.people: All reports carded on this shelf.
cards.result: The direction is consistent across the ICS-dependent trials (Bone 1989; Rebuck 1990), the small bronchodilator-maintained trial (Fairfax 1988, n=30) and the very small steroid-resistant trial (Marin 1996; 26 randomised, N=12 nedocromil completers, never load-bearing). Effect sizes are modest diary and lung-function differences over 4 weeks to 3 months. Nedocromil was withdrawn from several markets for commercial rather than safety reasons, which limits the practical reach of this record.
cards.watchOut: See the individual cards for each trial's limits — above all the era (1988–1996) and the small samples; this synthesis adds no new data.

shelves.title: Intrapleural streptokinase for pleural infection (MIST1): the large trial was negative (31% vs 27% death or surgery); pooled small-trial benefits vanish in low-bias sensitivity analysis
shelves.question: In adults with parapneumonic effusion or empyema, does intrapleural streptokinase (or another fibrinolytic alone) versus placebo or conservative management reduce death, surgical referral and hospital stay?
shelves.mesh: Anti-Bacterial Agents · Bacterial Infections · Combined Modality Therapy · Community-Acquired Infections · Cross Infection · Double-Blind Method · Drainage · Empyema, Pleural · Female · Fibrinolytic Agents · Humans · Instillation, Drug · Length of Stay · Lung · Male · Middle Aged · Pleural Diseases · Pneumonia · Radiography · Streptokinase · United Kingdom
shelves.balance: SPLIT — a large negative trial against a tail of small positive older trials, presented plainly and not pooled away. MIST1, the definitive trial of intrapleural streptokinase ALONE (454 randomised), found no difference in death or surgical drainage at 3 months (31% vs 27%; relative risk 1.14, 95% CI 0.85 to 1.54) and no benefit for mortality, surgery rate, radiographic outcome or hospital stay. The Cochrane syntheses, which pool MIST1 with the older small streptokinase/urokinase trials, find fewer surgical interventions with fibrinolysis (2019: odds ratio 0.37, 95% CI 0.21 to 0.68, low certainty) but no mortality difference — and in the 2019 sensitivity analysis confined to low/unclear risk-of-bias trials, the surgery and treatment-failure benefits disappeared. This shelf is fibrinolytic ALONE only: the tPA-plus-DNase combination question (MIST2) is homed at live #816, is cross-pointed here in prose, and none of its studies are re-carded on this shelf.

cards.headline: MIST1 (Maskell 2005): intrapleural streptokinase did NOT improve the primary outcome — death or surgical drainage at 3 months occurred in 31% on streptokinase versus 27% on placebo (relative risk 1.14, 95% CI 0.85 to 1.54; P=0.43)
cards.summary: MIST1 (Maskell 2005): intrapleural streptokinase did NOT improve the primary outcome — death or surgical drainage at 3 months occurred in 31% on streptokinase versus 27% on placebo (relative risk 1.14, 95% CI 0.85 to 1.54; P=0.43)
cards.type: Multicentre double-blind randomised controlled trial (MIST1), intrapleural streptokinase vs placebo in pleural infection
cards.people: 454 patients with pleural infection (purulent pleural fluid, or pleural fluid pH <7.2 with signs of infection, or proven bacterial invasion of the pleural space) were randomly assigned in this UK double-blind trial to intrapleural streptokinase 250,000 IU twice daily for 3 days or placebo, alongside antibiotics, chest-tube drainage, surgery and other routine care; 427 patients received streptokinase or placebo and were analysed for the primary endpoint (206 streptokinase, 221 placebo).
cards.result: There was no significant difference in the proportion who died or needed surgical drainage at 3 months: 64 of 206 (31%) with streptokinase versus 60 of 221 (27%) with placebo (relative risk 1.14, 95% CI 0.85 to 1.54; P=0.43) — a result the authors state excluded a clinically significant benefit of streptokinase. There was no benefit for mortality, rate of surgery, radiographic outcomes or length of hospital stay analysed separately. Serious adverse events (chest pain, fever or allergy) were more common with streptokinase (7% vs 3%; relative risk 2.49, 95% CI 0.98 to 6.36; P=0.08).
cards.watchOut: The definitive trial for streptokinase alone, and negative: it was designed precisely because the earlier small trials lacked power for clinical outcomes. It does not address fibrinolytic-plus-DNase combinations — that is the MIST2 question, homed at live #816 and not re-carded here.
cards.source: Maskell NA et al. U.K. Controlled trial of intrapleural streptokinase for pleural infection. The New England journal of medicine. 2005. PMID: 15745977. Registry ID: none in the record. cards.headline: Cochrane 2008 (Cameron): pooling 7 trials (761 participants), fibrinolysis reduced surgical intervention (relative risk 0.63, 95% CI 0.46 to 0.85) but not death (relative risk 1.08, 95% CI 0.69 to 1.68) — with explicit discordance between the earlier positive studies and the negative Maskell (MIST1) study
cards.summary: Cochrane 2008 (Cameron): pooling 7 trials (761 participants), fibrinolysis reduced surgical intervention (relative risk 0.63, 95% CI 0.46 to 0.85) but not death (relative risk 1.08, 95% CI 0.69 to 1.68) — with explicit discordance between the earlier positive studies and the negative Maskell (MIST1) study
cards.type: Cochrane systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised trials, intrapleural fibrinolytic therapy (streptokinase/urokinase) vs conservative management
cards.people: Systematic review of 7 randomised controlled trials in 761 adults with post-pneumonic empyema or complicated parapneumonic effusions without prior surgical intervention or trauma, comparing an intrapleural fibrinolytic agent (streptokinase or urokinase) via intercostal chest drain versus control, or the two agents against each other; searches to November 2006.
cards.result: In trials of patients with loculation and empyema, there was no significant difference in risk of death with fibrinolytics (relative risk 1.08, 95% CI 0.69 to 1.68). For treatment failure measured as surgical intervention, fibrinolytics reduced the risk (relative risk 0.63, 95% CI 0.46 to 0.85), but the reviewers stress the discordance between the earlier positive studies and the more recent negative Maskell study, and that a subgroup analysis of loculated/septated effusions suggested possible benefit only with incomplete data, not significant in the high-quality (Cochrane Grade A) subgroup. Fibrinolytics were not shown to significantly increase adverse events, but the confidence interval was too wide to exclude harm.
cards.watchOut: This synthesis INCLUDES MIST1 among its 7 trials — it is not evidence independent of the card above, and its pooled surgery benefit is driven by the smaller earlier trials that MIST1 contradicted. It covers fibrinolytic agents alone; combination therapy with DNase is a different question (live #816).
